transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO, Meridian), Marco Ruiz (Head of Security, Meridian), Claire Jensen (PM, Meridian)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through data residency and region-pinning options. Customer is in healthcare space and requires EU-only processing for certain datasets, plus audit log retention and KMS encryption. Discussion focused on hosted vs dedicated vs private options, sub-processors, cross-border processing rules, and SSO/RBAC integration. Action items captured to share SOC 2/ISO docs, network diagrams, and proposed region pinning configs.

Topics: data residency, region pinning, cross-border processing, sub-processors, KMS/encryption, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, VPC/private deployment

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samantha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick intro, I'm Samantha, I'm the AE on this deal and with me is Daniel our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Daniel (Redwood SE): hi all, daniel here, i'll be talking through the technical parts mostly.
[00:17] Priya (Meridian CTO): thanks, Samantha, hi Daniel. we pulled together a handful of folks because data residency is kind of a hard requirement for us across EU clinical data.
[00:26] Marco (Meridian Sec): yes we need to be explicit about region pinning, cross-border prevents any PHI leaving EU for certain patient records, and we need to understand sub-processors.
[00:36] Claire (PM): also curious about what happens during failover and backups, like if there's a cross-region failover does that trigger cross-border processing?
[00:46] Samantha: great question, we'll cover failover behavior, backups, and what we can guarantee for EU-only processing. quick agenda: go over certs (SOC2/ISO), KMS options, region pinning mechanics, sub-processor list, and next steps.
[00:58] Daniel: (slides shared link: https://redwood.example/sec/deck) okay starting with region pinning. Redwood supports hosted EU-only processing for customers who require data residency. basically requests from EU routes to EU pools, and where required we can pin workloads to EU-only capacity.
[01:15] Marco: when you say pin, is that at project-level, model-level, or route-level? we need per-environment pinning ideally so prod eu stays in eu while test can be global.
[01:28] Daniel: we can pin at route or project level, we also have an isolation option with Dedicated pools in a region. project-level pinning is what most enterprise customers use for strict residency.
[01:40] Priya: can you confirm backups and snapshots are stored in-region as well? we cannot have backups exported outside EU for those datasets.
[01:49] Daniel: yes, for pinned workloads backups and KV cache snapshots can be configured to remain in-region, we also encrypt at rest using KMS. note though, if you want customer-managed keys we support KMS integrations—AWS KMS and customer HSMs via a supported connector.
[02:05] Marco: ok so CMK support yes? we need to ensure Redwood never has plaintext access to our master keys.
[02:12] Samantha: correct, we offer envelope encryption where the customer-managed key is used to wrap data keys, and Redwood holds only the wrapped keys. Daniel can follow up with the integration diagram.
[02:23] Daniel: i'll draw that up in the network/KMS diagram, there are two patterns: hosted with CMK (Redwood calls KMS each key op) or private deployment where keys stay inside customer's VPC/HSM.
[02:36] Claire: what about cross-border processing for metadata or telemetry, is that considered data subject to the residency requirement?
[02:44] Marco: yes we need to know which telemetry is exported. some telemetry is fine but not clinical identifiers.
[02:50] Daniel: we can configure telemetry redaction and control which logs cross borders. audit logs for compliance can be retained in-region per your retention policy. by default some analytics aggregate in our central system, but for pinned workloads that aggregation can be scoped to the region or disabled entirely.
[03:07] Priya: do you have attestation or third-party audit proving that aggregation is disabled or scoped?
[03:13] Samantha: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate. those docs include control descriptions; we'll also share a sub-processor list.
[03:23] Marco: please include the current list of cloud sub-processors, particularly for EU region, and note any CDNs or monitoring vendors.
[03:31] Daniel: noted, we'll include that. Also to call out, for Dedicated we can offer physical isolation of capacity and separate tenancy which simplifies audit.
[03:41] Claire: can you clarify the failover behavior — if eu region degrades do you auto-fail to us-east or do you have a policy to keep requests queued?
[03:50] Daniel: policy-based. you can select strict residency which prevents cross-region failover — in that case requests will fail or queue until eu capacity recovers. Alternatively, you can configure a fallback to a compatible EU model variant in a different eu zone. we don't default to us-east for pinned workloads.
[04:08] Marco: what about sub-processors in the EU that may themselves have cross-border flows? we need full visibility.
[04:15] Samantha: we'll provide details on sub-processors and data flow maps. for anything that triggers cross-border we can flag and discuss mitigations.
[04:24] Priya: on encryption in transit, are you using mTLS between customer VPC and Redwood?
[04:29] Daniel: yes, we support mTLS for private links and TLS 1.3 for public endpoints. for VPC/private deployments there's a private peering model with mTLS and customer-controlled routing.
[04:41] Claire: SSO — we use SAML with SCIM provisioning. can Redwood integrate with our IdP and respect RBAC groups so only specific users can access EU-pinned routes?
[04:51] Daniel: absolutely, RBAC maps to IdP groups via SCIM, and route-level permissions are supported. we also write user-level audit trails.
[05:00] Marco: audit logs: what fields are captured and for how long? we need 7 years retention for certain logs per our compliance.
[05:07] Daniel: default audit event retention is 90 days in the console, but for enterprise we can set custom retention and export to your archive bucket (in-region) for long-term storage. we'll capture request metadata, user id, route, model version, token counts, and operation results; content-level logging is optional and can be redacted.
[05:27] Priya: about content logging, is it opt-in and can we prevent content storage entirely for EU patient records?
[05:33] Samantha: yes content logging is opt-in; for strict PHI workloads we recommend disabling content logging and enabling structured outputs only with ephemeral KV caches as needed.
[05:42] Claire: any third-party penetration tests or vulnerability reports we can review?
[05:47] Samantha: we have third-party pentest summaries and vulnerability management reports. i'll include summary and contacts. full reports may require an NDA.
[05:56] Marco: also need to understand sub-processor contract language — do you accept DPAs with EU SCCs or equivalent?
[06:03] Daniel: yes, we have a standard DPA that includes SCCs and we can negotiate addenda for enterprise legal terms.
[06:10] Priya: regarding on-prem options, can we run the inference runtime in our data center and keep telemetry completely internal?
[06:17] Daniel: yes that's our Private deployment offering. runtime can be installed behind your firewall, control plane can be customer-managed, and telemetry optionally routed to your monitoring stack. that said, Private comes with increased ops responsibilities on your side.
[06:29] Claire: what's the onboarding timeline for Private? we have regulatory windows to satisfy.
[06:33] Samantha: typical Private onboarding 6-10 weeks depending on infra readiness and compliance checks; Dedicated is faster for many customers. we'll follow up with a project plan.
[06:43] Marco: who are your EU sub-processors? please be specific.
[06:47] Daniel: current EU sub-processors include CloudFabric EU region (managed infra), LogStream EU (optional log aggregator), and CDN partners — we'll provide the list with descriptions and contact points.
[06:58] Priya: about cross-border for backups — if we have long-term archives are those stored under our control?
[07:03] Daniel: yes you can configure archive exports to your own encrypted S3 bucket in the EU, controlled by your KMS key. Redwood will not copy archives outside of the designated region unless explicitly authorized.
[07:16] Samantha: to recap, we'll send SOC 2/ISO, sub-processor list, KMS integration doc, and region-pinning diagram. Daniel will produce the network and KMS diagrams.
[07:27] Claire: great, and we'll assemble our list of data classes that must stay in EU and share by Friday.
[07:33] Marco: one last question, does Redwood support pseudonymization at ingestion so PHI is tokenized before it leaves our environment?
[07:41] Daniel: we have recommendations for pseudonymization pipelines and we can integrate with your tokenization service; for Private deployments this can be enforced locally.
[07:50] Priya: ok thanks, that covers most of it.
[07:54] Samantha: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed configurations. any final questions?
[08:00] Claire: none from me.
[08:02] Marco: no, thank you.
[08:04] Daniel: thanks all.
